note: Lithium cell chemistry reference data (P1 §5). Each chemistry is a Chemistry entity with nominal voltage, cell-level energy density, cycle life and temperature window — all expressed as typical ranges with a source annotation, per the site's no-number-without-evidence rule. Values vary by manufacturer, cell format and C-rate; they are not a substitute for a specific cell datasheet. LFP/NMC/NCA/LTO figures are cross-verified against the main-site lithium knowledge base and cell-manufacturer datasheets; LMFP is an emerging chemistry with a wider vendor spread (lower confidence).

chemistries.name: LFP
chemistries.evidence_note: Typical ranges; vary by manufacturer, cell format and C-rate. Energy density is cell-level — pack level is lower.

chemistries.name: NMC
sources: Cell-manufacturer datasheets (LG Energy Solution, Samsung SDI, CATL, Panasonic)
chemistries.evidence_note: Typical ranges; the exact nickel/manganese/cobalt ratio (e.g. NMC 811 vs 111) moves both energy density and cycle life.

chemistries.name: NCA
chemistries.evidence_note: Typical ranges; NCA is concentrated in cylindrical cells and holds a small energy-density edge over NMC.

chemistries.name: LTO
chemistries.thermal_stability: Very high (no metallic lithium plating; wide low-temp charge window)
chemistries.evidence_note: Lowest energy density and voltage of the group, but the longest cycle life and the widest charge-temperature window. Values are typical ranges.

chemistries.name: LMFP
sources: Cell-manufacturer datasheets (Gotion, CATL — early LMFP lines)
chemistries.evidence_note: Emerging chemistry with a wider vendor spread — treat energy-density and cycle-life figures as indicative rather than settled. Higher manganese content raises nominal voltage and energy density versus LFP.
